app.title: HydroPredict Hyderabad – station water-balance exploration and forecasting
app.summary: A person picks a monitoring station from a network loaded from a workbook, then looks over every station on a map and in a summary table. For the chosen station they read its rainfall, evaporation and cumulative water balance over time. They choose a variable, a horizon, a context window and a forecast strategy, then run a forecast. Before the forecast is shown, the foundation model, a seasonal baseline and a persistence baseline are each scored on a recent holdout, and the person gets a forecast with an uncertainty band plus a table comparing the methods. A live 10-day weather forecast for the station's coordinates is shown alongside for short-range context.

task.text: Explore daily rainfall, evaporation and water-balance records across a network of stations, and forecast one station's variable ahead after checking candidate methods against a recent holdout.

data.text: Daily weather records (rainfall, evaporation, max and min temperature) for a small network of stations with coordinates, plus derived net and cumulative water balance and a fetched 10-day weather forecast.
data.item: a station's daily record of one hydrological variable

stage.text: exploring station hydrology records and forecasting ahead from them

mechanism.text: Sidebar controls choose the station, variable and forecast settings, and every tab redraws for that choice: a map and table summarize the whole network, line charts show the station's history, and a button runs a holdout backtest and forecast whose method scores, ensemble weights and band are shown together. A separate tab fetches a live weather forecast for the same station's coordinates.

field.text: time-series forecasting of station water balance in hydrology

workflow.name: forecast a series ahead after scoring candidate methods on a recent holdout

steps.here: A bundled workbook with one sheet per station is loaded at start, and net water balance (rainfall minus evaporation) and its running total are computed for each station.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A map plots every station, coloured and sized by its ending cumulative water balance, above a network table of totals and averages per station.
Selecting a station in the sidebar fills metric cards and draws 30-day rolling rainfall against evaporation, plus the cumulative water balance as a storage-trend proxy.

steps.step: choose what to compute and how
steps.here: Sliders set the prediction horizon and historical context window, and dropdowns choose the variable and the strategy: weighted ensemble, foundation model only, best recent MAE, seasonal or persistence.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Run Forecast & Backtest holds out the most recent days, scores each candidate method on them, weights the ensemble by inverse MAE with bias correction, and plots the forecast with a 10th–90th percentile band and a table of values.
A backtest table sets the methods against each other on MAE, RMSE, bias and horizon-sum error, next to the best recent method and the ensemble weights.

steps.step: set the result against outside context
steps.here: A live 10-day ECMWF forecast for the station's coordinates is shown as rain bars and temperature lines, with expected rainfall totals and a rule-based recharge outlook.

distinctive: A foundation model is used zero-shot and is always scored against seasonal-climatology and persistence baselines on a recent holdout before its forecast is trusted.
Error is reported as horizon-total error as well as daily error, because water balance accumulates, so a forecast can do well day by day and still get the total wrong.
Cumulative rainfall minus evaporation is used as a stand-in for groundwater storage, since the data has no measured water-table depth.
Forecasts are clipped at zero when the history is never negative, and bands for non-model strategies come from the holdout residuals.
